findings.title: No cost- or memory-budgeted gate script reaches the coordinator cycle; a 2x loop-thread regression there is invisible
findings.claim: tests/stress.py is the only gate script that budgets CPU or memory, and its measured closure (tests/closures.json) holds none of coordinator.py, sensor.py, process_worker.py, price_model.py or narrative.py. So a change there does not select stress.py under GATE_SCOPE=auto, and on FULL it runs nothing in them. Injecting a second _build_data_dict per cycle raised loop-thread CPU per cycle from 0.257 to 0.363 reference solves (+41 %), and no budgeted check can see that increase.
findings.mechanism: stress.py drives HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize directly (build_case -> optimize) and never builds a HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator. Per-cycle work on the loop thread is not measured by any gate script: _async_update_data, _build_data_dict, _forecast_arrays, entity attribute rendering, and the pickle transport to the process worker. The same holds for memory the coordinator retains across cycles and for published payload bytes. structure.py prints a thread_factor but budgets no runtime quantity.

evidence.unit: budgeted gate scripts whose measured closure contains coordinator.py (also 0 for sensor.py, process_worker.py, price_model.py and narrative.py; positive control optimizer.py = 1)
evidence.machine: 4-vCPU shared cloud Linux container (not the M1 audit box), python 3.11.15, numpy 2.4.6 OpenBLAS, threads pinned to 1
evidence.contention_note: count; contention-immune. The companion loop-CPU ratio (s2_cycle.py) was taken at load1 14-24 alongside up to 13 seats, so it is provisional

findings.instrumented_symbol: tests/closure.py:select (measured closure table tests/closures.json) + heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._build_data_dict (driven through ._async_update_data on a real loop, s2_cycle.py)

perturbation.change: (a) s2_gate_blind.py --make-perturbed appends coordinator.py to tests/stress.py's closure, which is the fix shape: a budgeted script that exercises the cycle. (b) The companion arm s2_cycle.py --inject-build 2 runs _build_data_dict twice per call.
perturbation.observed_value: (a) budgeted_scripts_seeing_coordinator 0 -> 1; (b) loop_cpu_share_of_reference 0.2572 -> 0.3630 (loop_cpu_per_cycle 43.69 -> 56.38 ms, provisional), while the scoped gate still prints 'SKIP tests/stress.py' for coordinator.py

findings.metric_definition: Number of gate scripts that contain an elapsed-CPU or memory instrument and list the changed production file in their measured closure in tests/closures.json.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every production file on the per-cycle coordinator path (loop-thread work, retained collections, payload build, worker transport) must lie in the measured closure of at least one gate script that budgets CPU or memory for that path, so that a 2x regression there fails a check.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round8/D9/s2_gate_blind.py  (seams are the production files it lists with count 0; extend CYCLE_FILES to cover any module imported by coordinator.py)

null_control.command: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round8/D9/s2_cycle.py --cycles 30 --no-rss   (vs the same with --inject-build 2)
null_control.value: 0.2572 (null) vs 0.3630 (injected) loop CPU per cycle / reference_solve thread CPU
null_control.note: Both arms ran back to back in one session at a similar load (load1 ~14-24). The ratio moves with the injection; the absolute ms are about 4x the uncontended direct timings (build_data_dict 2.3 ms and forecast_arrays 1.3 ms measured alone) and are provisional.

reproduction_steps: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/closure.py select --files custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py  # prints SKIP tests/stress.py
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Add a cycle arm to the stress gate, or a new budgeted lane: drive N real _async_update_data cycles (real loop, real executor, worker route) and budget three quantities against the recorded table with the gate's existing ratio discipline. The three are loop-thread CPU per cycle as a ratio to reference_solve, the tracemalloc slope over cycles after warm-up, and the JSON bytes of recorded entity attributes. Its closure then carries coordinator.py and the files it imports. s2_cycle.py is a starting point.

non_findings.claim: The stress gate as shipped detects a synthetic exact-2x solve regression (HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize run twice per call, this tree only): 4 of 83 checks fail and rc=1. The work-count channels read exactly 2.00x against the uninjected HEAD^1 baseline captured in the same run (the null arm; 51 of 51 scenarios had unchanged plans). The failing checks are the evaluation count, the simulate count, the sweep ratio (210.62x vs 134.32x) and the per-scenario ceiling (1678x vs 1630x).
non_findings.command: python3 tests/gate_lock.py take --label D9-s2 && PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub GOLDEN_REF=HEAD^1 python3 tools/audit/round8/D9/s2_stress_2x.py --inject 2
non_findings.value: stress_rc=1; 4 of 83 checks failed; work ratio 2.00x (904/452 evals, 4234264/2117132 simulate step-equivalents on flat/1z/dhw); wall 2902 s (provisional, load1 7-25)

non_findings.claim: Loop-thread work per real coordinator cycle is small. It is about 0.26-0.31 of one reference solve under heavy contention, and about 9-12 ms in the first uncontended exploratory cycles. The biggest components timed alone are _build_data_dict at 2.3 ms, _forecast_arrays at 1.3 ms, and rendering all 74 entities' state and attributes at 4.4 ms. Pi extrapolation, assuming a Pi 4 core is 3-4x slower than this vCPU: roughly 30-50 ms of loop work per 15-minute cycle.
non_findings.value: loop_cpu_share_of_reference=0.3135 (median of cycles 9-112; 49.06 ms at load1 14.6, provisional); thread_factor 1.005

non_findings.claim: Retained bytes across cycles are bounded. The only coordinator attribute that grows is _accuracy (AccuracyTracker.samples deque maxlen=672, lead_pending capped at 512). The traced slope falls from 1654 to 1161 B/cycle between the first and second half of 112 cycles, and ru_maxrss in a fresh child is identical after 16 and after 112 cycles. Perturbation: accuracy.HISTORY_LENGTH=20 cuts the second-half slope to 729 B/cycle (down), so the harness sees the trim.
non_findings.value: traced_slope_second_half=1161 B/cycle (cap 20: 729); rss_slope=0 B/cycle (102984 kB at 16 and at 112 cycles, provisional)

non_findings.claim: Published payload stays within the recorder exclusion set. Across 74 entities, 8174 B of attributes per cycle are recorded and 79030 B are excluded by _unrecorded_attributes. The largest recorded set, the climate entity at 773 B, is far under the recorder's 16384 B per-state attribute cap. The large plan lists (space_heating_plan and dhw_heating_plan, about 23.5 kB each, and dhw_schedule at 6.6 kB) are all excluded. The worst case of about 0.8 MB/day assumes every recorded attribute set changes every cycle (96 cycles/day), before HA's attribute-hash dedup. _build_data_dict is 75.8 kB of JSON and is not recorded.
non_findings.value: recorded 8174 B/cycle, excluded 79030 B/cycle, max recorded 773 B/entity, data dict 75800 B

non_findings.claim: The worker transport per solve is small: the pickled job sent by coordinator:_run_in_process is 12997 B, the reply 16707 B, and the parent's executor-thread CPU is at most 1.3 ms per solve.

The stress memory pass probes 6 of 51 scenarios. This limit is stated in stress.py itself (#949 trade) and is not a new defect. On this Linux box, all 6 probes read at the empty-probe import floor (100.4 MiB), so attributable RSS is 0.0 MiB for every probe and only the traced axis can judge. This is a lead, not a finding: I injected no RSS-only regression.
non_findings.value: 6 of 6 probes at the import floor; traced 2.0-3.5 MiB against a recorded 1.8-3.5
